sources.cite: AWS Certified AI Practitioner (AIF-C01) exam guide: Fundamentals of AI and ML 20%, Fundamentals of Generative AI 24%, Applications of Foundation Models 28%, Guidelines for Responsible AI 14%, Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions 14%
sources.note: On 2026-11-17 a summarizing fetch of the AWS domain 3 page returned only page metadata, so the official text was not read. A third-party study guide (dennisk.neocities.org/aws_ai/domain3-study-guide.html, read the same day) gives Domain 3 as 28% and lists under Task 3.2 prompt injection or hijacking, jailbreaking, prompt poisoning and data exposure. The domain weights and objective wording are the course seed's (backend/supabase/seed/tracks/aws.ts). To verify against the AWS page.

sources.cite: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 (LLM01 Prompt Injection, LLM02 Sensitive Information Disclosure, LLM05 Improper Output Handling, LLM06 Excessive Agency, LLM08 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses)
sources.note: Relevant text: LLM01: 'Indirect prompt injections occur when an LLM accepts input from external sources, such as websites or files'; mitigations: constrain model behavior, enforce least privilege, 'Require human approval for high-risk actions', 'Separate and clearly denote untrusted content', filter inputs and outputs; scenario #2: hidden instructions make the model insert an image linking to an attacker-controlled URL, exfiltrating the conversation. LLM06 root causes: excessive functionality, permissions and autonomy; 'Utilise human-in-the-loop control to require a human to approve high-impact actions'. LLM08: 'Implement fine-grained access controls and permission-aware vector and embedding stores'. Read through summarizing fetches of genai.owasp.org on 2026-11-11.

sources.cite: NIST AI 100-1, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, January 26, 2023), and the Generative AI Profile NIST AI 600-1 (July 26, 2024)
sources.note: Relevant text: MANAGE 2.4 'Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use'; MANAGE 4.3 'Incidents and errors are communicated to relevant AI actors, including affected communities'. Read in the AI 100-1 PDF text and on the NIST page on 2026-11-11; the page notes AI RMF 1.0 'is being revised'.

sources.cite: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3, Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management: A CSF 2.0 Community Profile (April 2025)
sources.note: The current revision (April 3, 2025; supersedes Rev. 2 of 2012). Relevant text: RS.MA-02 'Perform a preliminary review of a new incident report to verify that a cybersecurity incident has occurred, then estimate the severity of the incident and the level of urgency'; RS.MA-03 'Prioritize how quickly incident response should be performed for each incident based on its scope, likely impact, time-critical nature, and resource availability'; RS.MA-04 escalation and elevation; RS.MI-01 'Containment refers to preventing the expansion of an incident'; RS.MI-02 eradication 'to eliminate persistence mechanisms and entry points' and 'Identify all affected hosts and services'; RS.AN-07 incident data collected with integrity and provenance preserved; RS.CO-02 stakeholders notified. Read in the PDF text (nvlpubs.nist.gov) and the CSRC page on 2026-11-11.

sources.cite: CrowdStrike, 2026 Global Threat Report (press release, 2026-02-24): 'The average eCrime breakout time fell to just 29 minutes in 2025', the fastest observed 27 seconds
sources.note: Vendor telemetry, not a standard. Also: '42% of vulnerabilities were exploited before public disclosure'; adversaries injected malicious prompts into GenAI tools at more than 90 organizations. Used only to set the scale of the attacker's clock; the scenario's step times are the author's. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-11.
